news_summary: AI technology is being effectively used in Somalia to improve food delivery and support hungry families.
news_summary_fr: En Somalie, l'intelligence artificielle est mise à profit pour améliorer la distribution de denrées alimentaires et venir en aide aux familles en situation de précarité alimentaire.
news_summary_es: En Somalia se está utilizando de forma eficaz la tecnología de inteligencia artificial para mejorar la distribución de alimentos y ayudar a las familias que padecen hambre.

articles.title: In Somalia, AI is helping deliver food to hungry families
articles.summary: Amid a deepening hunger crisis in Somalia, artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to deliver aid to the people who need it most.
articles.content:
Although the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) cannot reach all 6 million Somalis facing hunger, data collected by its partners and analysed through AI tools in its hunger-tracking platform HungerMap Live help the agency position resources in specific areas before conditions deteriorate. Somalia faces climate change-induced droughts followed by flash floods and a brutal conflict that has persisted for 35 years and killed hundreds of thousands. The Horn of Africa country also imports most of its food, exposing it to global price shocks such as the current conflict in the Middle East. © WFP/Sara Cuevas Gallardo

In June, WFP and the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) added Somalia to their list of “hunger hotspots of highest concern” alongside northeast Nigeria, joining Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen and Palestine. “It is a very gruesome situation, and I’m very, very concerned about these next few weeks and months,” said Simon Renk, head of vulnerability, analysis and mapping for the WFP in Somalia. Tweet URL Using AI in Burhakaba In the Burhakaba District, about 180 kilometres northwest of the capital, Mogadishu, dangerously malnourished children fill local medical centres. WFP’s humanitarian workers identified the district’s urgent need using the AI tools in HungerMap Live. Armed with that knowledge, the agency provided food assistance to 48,000 people and nutrition support to 3,000 women and children. “Instead of waiting for that malnutrition of children to deteriorate and lead to displacement or even death, we knew it prior,” Mr. Renk told UN News. Old technology, new lifesaving potential First launched in January 2020 to monitor food security in more than 90 countries, HungerMap Live is a publicly-accessible platform that uses data on food insecurity, climate, economies, agriculture, inflation and more to display areas that are currently food insecure or moving in that direction. Although that initial version of HungerMap Live used AI to estimate levels of food insecurity in countries lacking sufficient data, its ability to predict future hunger crises was limited and it did not track the nutritional quality of diets in the countries it tracks. Enter HungerMap Live 2.0. Released by WFP in April, the update overhauled the user interface and introduced new predictive AI features, allowing governments and WFP field offices around the world to mobilise resources and act before a crisis worsens. © WFP/Sara Cuevas Gallardo

articles.personality_title: AI helps deliver food aid to hungry families in Somalia
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Somalia is facing a serious hunger crisis caused by droughts, floods, ongoing conflict, and rising food prices. About 6 million people in the country do not have enough to eat. The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) works to provide food but cannot reach everyone in need.

**What happened** – The WFP is using artificial intelligence (AI) through a tool called HungerMap Live to track where hunger is worst in Somalia. This helps them send food and nutrition support to the right places before the situation gets worse. For example, in the Burhakaba District near the capital Mogadishu, AI data showed a high risk of malnutrition. Because of this, WFP provided food for 48,000 people and special nutrition for 3,000 women and children.

**Impact** – Using AI allows aid workers to act faster and more precisely. Instead of waiting for hunger to cause serious illness or displacement, they can stop problems early. HungerMap Live collects many types of information like weather, food prices, and farming conditions to predict where hunger will rise. The newest version, launched in April, improved these predictions and made the tool easier to use.

**What’s next step** – The WFP and governments can use HungerMap Live 2.0 to better prepare and respond to hunger crises worldwide. This means food aid can reach more people before emergencies become worse. Continued updates and data will help make the system even more accurate.

**One-sentence takeaway** – AI technology is helping the World Food Programme deliver food aid in Somalia more quickly and precisely, preventing hunger and saving lives before crises deepen.
articles.personality_title_fr: L'IA aide à distribuer de la nourriture aux familles affamées en Somalie
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – La Somalie traverse une grave crise alimentaire causée par la sécheresse, les inondations, un conflit prolongé et la hausse des prix des aliments. Environ 6 millions de personnes manquent de nourriture. Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) des Nations Unies tente d’aider, mais ne peut pas atteindre tout le monde.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Le PAM utilise l’intelligence artificielle (IA) via un outil appelé HungerMap Live pour suivre où la faim est la plus forte en Somalie. Cela leur permet d’envoyer de la nourriture et un soutien nutritionnel aux endroits nécessaires avant que la situation ne s’aggrave. Par exemple, dans le district de Burhakaba près de Mogadiscio, l’IA a montré un risque élevé de malnutrition. Grâce à cela, le PAM a fourni de la nourriture à 48 000 personnes et un soutien nutritionnel à 3 000 femmes et enfants.

**Impact** – L’IA permet aux travailleurs humanitaires d’agir plus vite et avec plus de précision. Au lieu d’attendre que la faim cause des maladies graves ou des déplacements, ils peuvent prévenir ces problèmes. HungerMap Live collecte des données sur le climat, les prix, l’agriculture pour prédire où la faim va augmenter. La nouvelle version sortie en avril améliore ces prédictions et rend l’outil plus facile à utiliser.

**Prochaine étape** – Le PAM et les gouvernements pourront utiliser HungerMap Live 2.0 pour mieux préparer et répondre aux crises alimentaires dans le monde. Cela permettra d’atteindre plus de personnes avant que les urgences ne s’aggravent. Les mises à jour et données futures rendront le système encore plus précis.

**Résumé en une phrase** – La technologie IA aide le Programme alimentaire mondial à distribuer la nourriture plus rapidement et précisément en Somalie, prévenant la faim et sauvant des vies avant que la crise ne s’aggrave.
articles.personality_title_es: La IA ayuda a entregar alimentos a familias hambrientas en Somalia
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Somalia enfrenta una grave crisis de hambre causada por sequías, inundaciones, conflicto continuo y aumento de precios de alimentos. Cerca de 6 millones de personas no tienen suficiente comida. El Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) de la ONU trabaja para ayudar, pero no puede llegar a todos.

**Qué pasó** – El PMA usa inteligencia artificial (IA) con una herramienta llamada HungerMap Live para rastrear dónde el hambre es peor en Somalia. Esto les ayuda a enviar alimentos y apoyo nutricional a los lugares correctos antes de que la situación empeore. Por ejemplo, en el distrito de Burhakaba, cerca de Mogadiscio, la IA mostró un alto riesgo de desnutrición. Gracias a esto, el PMA entregó comida a 48,000 personas y apoyo nutricional a 3,000 mujeres y niños.

**Impacto** – La IA permite que los trabajadores humanitarios actúen más rápido y con mayor precisión. En vez de esperar a que el hambre cause enfermedades graves o desplazamientos, pueden prevenir esos problemas. HungerMap Live usa datos sobre clima, precios y agricultura para predecir dónde aumentará el hambre. La versión más reciente, lanzada en abril, mejoró estas predicciones y facilitó su uso.

**Próximo paso** – El PMA y los gobiernos podrán usar HungerMap Live 2.0 para prepararse y responder mejor a las crisis de hambre en todo el mundo. Esto significa que la ayuda alimentaria llegará a más personas antes de que las emergencias empeoren. Las actualizaciones futuras harán el sistema aún más preciso.

**Resumen en una frase** – La tecnología de IA está ayudando al Programa Mundial de Alimentos a entregar ayuda alimentaria en Somalia de forma más rápida y precisa, previniendo el hambre y salvando vidas antes de que la crisis empeore.
